clue.text: Van taking some Parisian round about hurried

indicators.note: round says the turned French word goes around the vehicle
about signals that the French word is turned back to front

parts.note: des is the French for 'some', as a Parisian would say it
a camper is a camper van, a van fitted out for living in

explanation.surface: A van picks up a French passenger and drives off around the place in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word is turned by 'about' before 'round' wraps it around the vehicle, so its letters split either side.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and lightly, so having scampered is having hurried.

clue.text: Tis, we deduce, to keep going beyond 15?

parts.note: in a down light, the word sit written upwards gives the letters of Tis

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader works out what the old poetic contraction means while pressing on past a certain point.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read 'Tis' as the result, and the instruction that makes it is SIT written UP the grid. 15 down is MIDNIGHT, so the definition means staying out of bed past midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit up is to stay awake and out of bed late, keeping going past the small hours.

clue.text: A star team beaten — bad play, actually

indicators.note: beaten, like eggs whisked up, signals the letters are mixed

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
a play is made of acts, and an act is a piece of theatre

explanation.surface: A star team has lost, and the commentator says plainly that they played badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges only A STAR TEAM; 'bad play' looks like a description of the match but supplies the last two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock synonym for in fact or really, used to correct or add a point.

clue.text: More than one saw an old book

definitions.meaning: a saw is an old saying or adage, so several are wise sayings
a book of the Old Testament of the Bible, traditionally linked to Solomon

explanation.surface: Someone looks over several cutting tools beside an antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws are adages, and the biblical book of that name collects such sayings.

clue.text: Possibly using electronic control to get volume turned up in bank

indicators.note: in places the turned book inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a volume is a book, a tome

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the TV volume can be raised with the remote while sitting in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads the book backwards, as fits a down light, and 'in' sets it inside the word for bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Done remotely means operated from a distance, as by a remote control handset.

clue.text: Various competitors at the Olympic Games?

definitions.meaning: an old word meaning several or sundry
people who plunge from springboards and platforms in an Olympic sport

explanation.surface: A sports writer notes the mixed range of athletes at the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry, and the noun names athletes in the Olympic diving events.

clue.text: Commander in endless agitation in centre of activity

indicators.note: in places the commander inside the shortened bother
endless says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a fuss is a state of agitated bother
OC stands for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A commanding officer finds himself in a constant state of upset at the heart of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts FUSS to FUS, and OC goes 'in' it: F-OC-US.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is a central point where activity or attention gathers.

clue.text: Growth of sport -—enthuse no end

parts.note: sport in the sense of fun or amusement

indicators.note: no end says the last letter is lost

parts.note: to gush is to enthuse effusively

explanation.surface: A sports fan's growing excitement is described as an expansion of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' takes the H off GUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mould or mushroom is an organic growth, such as appears on damp walls or skin.

clue.text: New mug is "correct," yes? It should be after this!

definitions.text: New mug is "correct," yes? It should be after this!

indicators.note: new signals that the following letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: After a facelift a patient admires their new face and asks if it is right.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug is slang for face. 'New' rearranges MUG IS CORRECT YES into the answer, and the whole clue describes the result of the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic operations to improve appearance are meant to leave the face new and corrected.

clue.text: We may avoid it under awning: pet hides under paper

definitions.text: We may avoid it under awning

indicators.note: in a down clue, hides under places the second piece below the first

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to pet an animal is to stroke it

explanation.surface: A cat shelters beneath a sunshade while its owner reads the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatstroke caused by too much sun is avoided by staying in shade such as an awning gives.

clue.text: Rush round to take order in cafe

parts.note: to tear is to rush along
round is the shape of the letter O
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A waiter hurries about taking customers' orders in a busy cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe and a tea shop are both small places serving light refreshments.

clue.text: Only half the cricket team is regularly taking meat

indicators.note: only half keeps the second three letters and drops the first three

parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players, so it is called an eleven
someone who is on a medicine takes it regularly

explanation.surface: Half a cricket team is said to be eating meat as a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat is called by this name in British and American kitchens alike.

clue.text: Sequence of words not right for the stage

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out

parts.note: a phrase is a short sequence of words

explanation.surface: An actor uses a wrong line of dialogue on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage of a process and a phase of it are both a distinct step or period.

clue.text: Blunt and true, in trouble like Becket?

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An outspoken, honest man gets into difficulty, as Thomas Becket did with the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry II is said to have called Archbishop Thomas Becket 'this turbulent priest' before his murder in 1170.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous phrase about Becket uses this adjective, meaning unruly and troublesome.

clue.text: Language of murder victim strangled by partner

indicators.note: strangled by puts the victim inside the partner, wrapped in

parts.note: a mate is a partner
Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A detective identifies the tongue of a person throttled by their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Ndebele people of Zimbabwe is also known by this older name.

clue.text: Sail low — new angle's right

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound a cow makes
a rake is a slope or angle, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A sailor sees a sail sitting low and a fresh angle that's just right.
explanation.definitionFit: A light topmost square sail flown above the skysail on old sailing ships has this name.

clue.text: Island party by lake or pool

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers choose between an island party by the lake or one at the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air public swimming baths is called by this Italian-derived name in Britain.

clue.text: I had name for being in power in a time of transition

indicators.note: being in places the first pieces inside the word for power

parts.note: might is power
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: A former leader recalls holding office during a changeover of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night marks the changeover from one day to the next.

clue.text: Spooner's fuel, rounded mass that could lead to room being warmed up

definitions.text: that could lead to room being warmed up

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: peat is dug and burnt as fuel
a hump is a rounded mass or lump

explanation.surface: A heap of fuel is piled in a corner to heat up a chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of PEAT and HUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that moves heat from outside air or ground into a building warms rooms.

clue.text: Brute with twisted personality overcoming resistance

indicators.note: overcoming puts one piece over and around the other
twisted says the word is turned round

parts.note: your ego is your sense of self or personality

explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns EGO into OGE, which goes around R.

clue.text: I can't see flicks? That's a hardship for me!

definitions.text: I can't see flicks? That's a hardship for me!

parts.words: I can't see flicks? That's a hardship for me!

explanation.surface: Someone laments being unable to go to the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A film enthusiast or devoted moviegoer, the word borrowed from French.

clue.text: One in political group establishing equality

parts.note: a party is a political group

explanation.surface: One member of a party campaigns for equal rights.

clue.text: Like many a lady-in-waiting in decline

ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen whom many such ladies served

clue.text: Correspondence about fine expansionary economic policy

clue.text: I sort out the new starters

clue.text: Second try is a strain

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: A second attempt puts someone under stress.

clue.text: Rascally jerk finally crashes his van

explanation.surface: A dishonest driver loses control and wrecks his van.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest and roguish, like a knave or scoundrel.

clue.text: Fellow eating third bit of tart before getting cheese

indicators.note: eating puts the picked letter inside the fellow

clue.text: Irritable, his friend being a dangerous driver

definitions.text: his friend being a dangerous driver
definitions.meaning: the Water Rat in The Wind in the Willows is friend of the reckless motorist Toad

clue.text: Think highly of actor spending pounds, old contributor to local community
